Implemented the Python Nushell compatibility port.

Changed:
- Added [nushell_port.py](/C:/Users/liuliu/Documents/tura_workspace/target/project-rebuild-source-port/r-9ad4ef9f48/nushell/codex-main-1/workspace/nushell_port.py)
- Added Python entrypoint [executable](/C:/Users/liuliu/Documents/tura_workspace/target/project-rebuild-source-port/r-9ad4ef9f48/nushell/codex-main-1/workspace/executable)
- Updated [compile.sh](/C:/Users/liuliu/Documents/tura_workspace/target/project-rebuild-source-port/r-9ad4ef9f48/nushell/codex-main-1/workspace/compile.sh) to recreate the Python entrypoint idempotently

Coverage includes `nu -c` expressions, lists/records/tables, JSON/CSV conversion, strings, math, common table commands, variables, and basic filesystem snippets.

Verification:
- `python -m py_compile ./nushell_port.py ./executable` passed.
- 50 reference comparisons matched byte-for-byte for exit status, stdout, and stderr.
- Final smoke test matched: `[[a b]; [1 2] [3 4]] | where a > 1 | to json --raw`.

One environment note: this Windows shell only exposes `C:\WINDOWS\system32\bash.exe`, which is a broken WSL launcher here, so I could not execute `compile.sh` locally through `sh`. The generated `executable` itself was verified directly with Python.
